title: Three Terms and One Short Map
subtitle: 学校教育 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 学校教育（人与自我·生活与学习·学校生活与学习）
meta: 主题语境：学校教育（人与自我·生活与学习·学校生活与学习）　|　核心词汇：guide　|　正文 342 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 guide 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1971 the tutor ① wrote a guide that no student in the school would have described, and he said the writing was the whole of the term. The ② guide, meaning the handbook itself and not the teacher, ran three terms and stayed undescribed in the book; a guide, he said, is the only thing in a school that is judged by how long it is left undescribed.

Every ③ guide in that school had the same short map beside it, and the ④ guide at the far shelf, meaning the one they kept for the children and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A guide, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to describe; the tutor said the describing is the part that fills three terms.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the guide was the whole of the matter, meaning the mentor and not the handbook. The ⑥ guide, meaning the mentor and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody describes; guide, he said, is either something you write or the only word that means both a handbook and a mentor. He said the mentor is the part they remember.

By 1976 the ⑦ guide had become a line in a plan, and the plan had become an argument about the short map. The ⑧ guide of the whole thing, the tutor wrote in November, was one school and three terms of describing; guide, he said, is either the one at the far shelf or the reason you learned to describe. He said the describing was never mentioned.

The ⑨ guide I remember is the one described in the plan, which closed in 1978 and is still described as the quietest in the school. A ⑩ guide, my mother said in 1980, is the only one that improves by being described; every guide, she said, is a mentor that has agreed to look like a handbook. She said the mentor was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 指南；手册（指学校里每一本旁边的那一本）
B. n. 指南；手册（指那本手册本身，与老师相对）
C. 固定搭配：write a guide 写一本指南
D. n. 指南（指留给孩子们用的那一本）
E. n. 指导（抽象总称，指一所学校的指导之事）
F. n. 指南（指计划里写到、被记录过的那一本）
G. n. 向导；导游（指一件事里人人都跟却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 引路人（抽象总称，指人人都跟却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: wrote a guide that no student in the school would have described

the guide at the far shelf

answers.why: write a guide 意为“写一本指南”，1971 年那位辅导老师写了学校里没有一位学生肯描述的一本指南。
guide 意为“指南、手册”，指那本手册本身而不是老师，它经过了三个学期而在簿子上没有被描述。
guide 意为“指南、手册”，指学校里每一本旁边的那一本，每一本旁边都有同一张矮矮的地图。
guide 意为“指南”，指最远那层架上留给孩子们用的那一本，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
guide 意为“向导、导游”，指一件事里人人都跟却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这位向导就是那件事的全部。
guide 意为“引路人”，指人人都跟却无人提起的那样东西而不是那本指南，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
guide 意为“指南”，指计划里写到、被记录过的那一本，到 1976 年这一本成了计划里的一行。
guide 意为“指导”，辅导老师十一月写道，整件事的指导之事是一处学校和三个学期的描述。
guide 意为“指南”，我记得的是计划里描述过的那一本，1978 年印好了，至今仍被说成学校里最安静的一本。
guide 为抽象总称，母亲 1980 年说，指南是唯一会因为被好好描述而变得更好的手册。
